title: RTP Analysis：Fix nominal and arrival times calculation
description:
Previously, the nominal and arrival times are calculated based on first packet
in the RTP stream, but there is a corner case: if the stream codec changes in the
middle, e.g., from AMR-WB to AMR, the nominal time will be calculated using the
current codec frequency, and it is not correct and will affect diff and jitter.

This fix will calculate nominal and arrival times based on previous in-sequence
RTP packet.

There is a test pcap file attached. In frame 11, the codec is changed from AMR-WB to AMR, and I use AMR frequency to calculate `nominaltime` for frame 11 (Maybe should use frame 10's frequency?). The following is test result:  
Before my patch: Frame 11 jitter is: 3.91; diff is 60.  
After my patch: Frame 11 jitter is: 1.41; diff is 20.

Please help to review it, thanks very much in advance! [rtp_multi_codec_test.pcap](/uploads/3554abb223fe6a57248393a18a917d5f/rtp_multi_codec_test.pcap)

notes.body: @j.novak When you are free, could you check this PR please? Thanks very much in advance!

  • 7e9329b2...3c944de9 - 5324 commits from branch wireshark:master

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/4853/diffs?diff_id=706182021&start_sha=7e9329b27d32cba5d05fbbaa8698a398b0887a52)

This broke #16330, though not for the example in the issue. (The example has packets excluded because they are before the first packet captured.)

`in_time_sequence` just checks if the timestamp looks plausible compared to the first timestamp, i.e. wouldn't give a negative number if the difference were interpreted as signed. It's not a test for "is packet N+1 in time sequence compared to packet N?" (Later tests for being in sequence number order catch this.)

That was fine when calculating jitter based on the first packet, but doesn't work when calculating based on previous packet if the new packet is earlier than the previous packet. The expected nominal arrival diff can be negative, but is being treated as unsigned.
